ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, banking, investment approval, and each material ownership or control change, screen all direct and indirect owners, directors, authorized representatives, senior managers, signatories, agents, and key counterparties against United Nations Security Council lists, Taiwan domestic sanctions and designated-terrorist lists, OFAC SDN and other relevant OFAC lists, PRC sanctions and export-control lists where legally relevant, and reputable commercial PEP and adverse-media databases. Identify domestic and foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates; obtain senior-management approval, establish source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, apply enhanced monitoring, and document false-positive resolution. Do not treat OFAC lists as automatically applicable Taiwan law; apply them contractually and for USD, US-person, correspondent-bank, cloud, and payment-rail exposure. Escalate suspected ML or terrorist financing to the Investigation Bureau, Ministry of Justice, and applicable financial institution compliance function.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs Department of Commerce Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Check System and the One-Stop Online Application Platform for Company, Business, and Limited Partnership Registration (official domains include gcis.nat.gov.tw and company.boss.gov.tw)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered Chinese company name must use legally accepted Chinese characters and comply with the Company Act and Ministry of Economic Affairs naming rules. An English name may be registered or used as permitted by the relevant filing process but does not replace the required Chinese name. The proposed name must be distinguishable from existing registered or reserved names and must not mislead the public regarding business type, governmental status, regulated activities, or relationship with another entity. The business scope must use permitted business-item classifications. A PRC-related investment or control structure requires separate investment approval and cannot be implemented solely through name reservation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying government, public authority, diplomatic status, or official agency status without statutory authorization
Words implying a bank, securities firm, futures enterprise, insurance enterprise, trust enterprise, financial holding company, or other regulated financial institution without the required license
Words implying a medical institution, hospital, clinic, pharmacy, laboratory, or healthcare provider where the entity will not hold the applicable health-sector authorization
Words implying a university, school, research institute, charity, foundation, or public-interest institution without legal basis
Words implying a national, central, official, international, or cross-border governmental character without approval
Names identical or confusingly similar to registered companies, trademarks, public bodies, or well-known enterprises
Words or expressions contrary to public order, morals, law, or mandatory naming rules
Terms associated with prohibited or restricted PRC political, military, or state organizations without authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain the written or electronic rejection reason from the Ministry of Economic Affairs Department of Commerce or the relevant local registration authority. Verify identical-name, confusing-similarity, business-scope, regulated-word, translation, and public-order grounds. Submit a corrected name pre-check application first where the issue is curable. If an appeal is legally available, file an administrative petition or appeal with the issuing authority within the stated statutory period, attach proof of distinctiveness, trademark or corporate-name rights, business-scope evidence, and all supporting corporate documents, and request a written decision. If the administrative decision remains adverse, consider an administrative litigation action under the Administrative Appeal Act and Administrative Litigation Act after Taiwan counsel confirms standing, deadline, and exhaustion requirements. Do not sign leases, advertise, open payment accounts, or incur regulated-business obligations based only on a rejected or unconfirmed name. The stated 30-day period must be verified against the live portal and current administrative notice because Taiwan name-reservation periods and electronic filing rules may change.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Taiwan company must maintain a registered office capable of receiving official notices and supporting registration. A serviced or virtual office may be accepted for a software company if the provider permits registration, the address is lawfully usable, and the company can demonstrate genuine management, records, communications, and operational capacity. A mailbox-only address, accommodation address, or address incapable of receiving inspections is high risk. For EMR cloud software, the entity must separately assess personal-data, cybersecurity, medical-device, cloud-hosting, patient-data, and payment-processor requirements. If the entity operates or markets a medical institution, provides clinical services, or supplies software qualifying as a medical device or software as a medical device, additional Ministry of Health and Welfare or Taiwan Food and Drug Administration approvals may apply. A virtual office does not replace required technical personnel, secure systems, data governance, or licensed clinical operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 10%-20% annual probability for an ordinary low-risk software company with a credible Taiwan address and complete filings; estimated 25%-40% during the first two years where the entity has PRC ownership or control, a regulated healthcare scope, foreign investment approval, unusual ownership layers, banking alerts, or inconsistent operational evidence. These are risk estimates, not statutory probabilities. Unannounced or short-notice inspections, document requests, address verification, tax inquiries, labor inspections, and sector-regulator reviews remain legally possible.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Companies Act (公司法), as amended, particularly Articles 1-18 (Incorporation), Article 128 (Promoters), Article 156 (Capital and Shares), Article 160 (Articles of Incorporation), and Article 387 (Filing Requirements); Foreign Investment Act (外國人投資條例) Articles 7-10 for JV approval
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs; One-Stop Company Registration and Operation Online (公司與商業一站式申請作業)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (公司章程) together with Company Establishment Registration Application (公司設立登記申請書)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited company in Taiwan; however, the authorized capital must be reasonably proportionate to the proposed business scope. Foreign investment capital must be remitted into a NT$ escrow account and certified by a Taiwan CPA prior to incorporation submission to MOEA Investment Commission (MOEAIC).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company adopts its Articles of Incorporation and authorizes the incorporation filing with the Ministry of Economic Affairs. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is established at [address in Taiwan]. RESOLVED, that the initial capital contribution of NT$[amount] is approved, and the Chairman and Directors are authorized to open bank accounts and manage all pre-registration matters. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as Chairman, [Name] as General Manager, and [Name] as Corporate Secretary, each to assume office upon issuance of the company registration certificate. RESOLVED, that the Corporate Secretary is directed to obtain all required industry and operational licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name and Business Scope Approval (Jaqueline Name Pre-Screening)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review System (公司名稱及所營事業預查)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application for company name pre-approval, providing two alternative Chinese names and the full proposed business scope (including ISIC 6201 'Electronic Medical Record Software Services' and 'Medical Information System Design and Development'). Pay NT$300. The approval certificate is valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Application form for name and business scope pre-approval
Identity documents of foreign promoters (passport copies)
Power of attorney for the representative if filed by agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or the scope is challenged, file a modification application within 5 business days, providing revised alternatives and a detailed classification reference (ISIC/Chinese Industrial Classification). If approval is not obtained, appeal to the MOEA Adjudication Committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Commission (FIC) Approval for JV Capital Structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Investment Commission (MOEAIC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an investment application to MOEAIC, supplying the JV contract, capital remittance plan, and shareholding structure. Capital must be remitted into an escrow account with a designated bank in Taiwan, and a CPA capital verification report is required. Obtain FIC approval letter before proceeding to registry.
required_dossiers: JV agreement and articles of incorporation draft
Financial statements or credit references of foreign investor
Proof of capital remittance and escrow account statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FIC raises questions regarding business scope or ownership, provide supplementary explanations and undertake to comply with local legal restrictions on medical software. If the application is denied, revise the JV structure (e.g., shareholding percentage) and resubmit through the FIC online portal within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarizing Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan District Court Notary Public or licensed Taiwan attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Chinese, covering company name, business scope (EMR SaaS and related IT services), total authorized capital, issued shares, director and supervisor provisions, and registered office address. The document must be signed by all founding promoters and notarized in Taipei.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the founders' meeting approving the articles
Power of attorney for the Taiwan representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests amendments (e.g., on business scope wording), revise the document and re-notarize. Delays are cured by ensuring both Chinese and English versions are consistent and include the exact ISIC 6201 description.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Verification and Bank Escrow Release
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary NT$ deposit account with a Taiwan bank under the company name (pre-registration). Deposit the full paid-up capital from the escrow account. The CPA issues a capital verification report (資本額查核報告書) after reviewing the bank deposit certificate and the approved Articles of Incorporation. Capital can only be released after company registration is completed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the capital verification fails due to currency exchange or proof issues, reconcile the remittance paperwork with MOEAIC. If the bank delays escrow release, provide the FIC approval and registration application to the bank's compliance department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA One-Stop Company Registration and Operation Online Portal (商業司一站式系統)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the electronic application with all required attachments, including the notarized Articles of Incorporation, FIC approval, capital verification report, and the first board resolution. The system assigns a company unified business number (統一編號). After validation, MOEA issues the Company Establishment Registration Certificate (公司登記證明書).
required_dossiers: Photocopy of ID/passport of directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA returns a deficiency notice, correct the specified item and re-submit within 15 days. If the certificate is withheld due to incomplete FIC or capital matters, coordinate with MOEAIC and CPA to resubmit the corrected version. No additional fee is charged for first correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation Registration: Tax Registration and Labor/Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local National Taxation Bureau (國稅局) and Bureau of Labor Insurance (勞工保險局)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after company registration, register for profit-seeking enterprise income tax filing, VAT (business tax), and withholding tax. Register the company with the Bureau of Labor Insurance, health insurance, and pension fund; also apply for stamp tax declaration. Obtain a unified invoice supplier certificate (統一發票購買證) if issuing invoices.
required_dossiers: Unified business number certificate (統一編號證)
Company seal and responsible person seal registration
Form to register for tax duties (申請營業稅籍登記)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed or queried, file a supplementary declaration with penalties waived for first-time small delays. If the business code assigned is not aligned with ISIC 6201, request a reclassification with supporting documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health and Welfare (MOHW), Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA) — Medical Device Division; Ministry of Economic Affairs, Industrial Development Administration (IDA) for software industry classification
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing License (醫療器材製造業許可執照) for SaMD (Software as a Medical Device) / Information Service Provider Registration for EMR Clinical Workflow Platform

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Executive Yuan (行政院環境保護署)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Exempt – Category C (Low Impact). Hotel and healthcare software services are not listed within mandatory EIA categories; only a simple environmental registration and waste disposal statement is required for office premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A for software-only operations. However, if the JV operates a demonstration clinic or data center, wastewater discharge must comply with Effluent Standards (放流水標準) under the Water Pollution Control Act (COD≤30 mg/L, SS≤30 mg/L, pH 6-9). VOC emissions from backup generators must meet EPA Air Pollution Control Act standards (e.g., NOx≤200 ppm, CO≤400 ppm). General office waste and e-waste (including server batteries) must be recycled via certified recyclers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification (消防安全設備檢修申報) — annual inspection by local fire department; Building User License (建築物使用執照) for office rental space, including staircase load compliance; Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA/Taiwan - 勞動部職業安全衛生署) workplace clearance for computer workstation ergonomics, electrical safety, and emergency evacuation planning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance of Taiwan (財政部), specifically the Taxation Agency (財政部賦稅署) and the regional National Taxation Bureaus (各地區國稅局) exercising direct collection and audit authority; official taxpayer e-service portal: https://www.tax.nat.gov.tw; official e-Invoice Integration Platform (電子發票整合服務平台): https://www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The foreign investors obtain investment approval from the Department of Investment Review of the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) in accordance with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals. Step 2: The JV is incorporated through the MOEA One-Stop Company Registration Service, which automatically issues the 8-digit Uniform Business Number (統一編號) that serves as the sole CIT/VAT tax identifier. Step 3: Within 15 days of business commencement, the entity files profit-seeking enterprise tax registration and VAT registration with the local National Taxation Bureau using the MOEA company registration certificate, articles of incorporation, the shareholders' register, the lease or title evidence for the Taiwan principal place of business, an executed certificate of the responsible person, and notarized powers of attorney of the non-resident directors. Step 4: The National Taxation Bureau activates the VAT 'business enterprise' (營業人) status and the Uniform Invoice (統一發票) issuance authorization. Step 5: The entity then registers the Turnkey e-Invoice API account and opens a foreign-currency deposit account with a licensed Taiwan foreign-exchange bank to earmark export proceeds for zero-rating refund substantiation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is a Taiwan tax-resident company limited by shares, subject to 20% corporate income tax on worldwide income; no pass-through or fiscal-transparent election is recognized for this entity type. Territorial_Scope — resident companies are taxable on worldwide profits; EMR SaaS foreign service income is assessable for CIT but zero-rated for VAT when used abroad; retained earnings undistributed are subject to an additional 5% entity-level retained earnings surtax under Article 21-1 of the Income Tax Act. Tax_Exempt_Zone — not applicable; the JV is a standard mainland-jurisdiction software company and cannot claim export processing zone, free trade zone, or offshore company concessions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists in Taiwan for a locally incorporated limited company. The available statutory elections relevant to this JV include: (i) the R&D expenditure tax-credit election under Article 10 of the Statute for Industrial Innovation (15% current-year credit capped at 30% of income tax payable, or an alternative 10% multi-year uncapped credit option); (ii) the foreign income tax credit election under Article 3 of the Income Tax Act for foreign-source EMR SaaS revenue; (iii) the zero-rated export invoice election under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act requiring documentary substantiation; (iv) the election to issue cloud e-invoices via the Turnkey automated transmission or certified value-added center API; and (v) no elective CFC/PEM arrangement is permitted — Articles 43-3 and 43-4 of the Income Tax Act mandate attribution/recharacterization of offshore controlled subsidiaries and offshore fixed places of business, supplemented by the substance-over-form clause of Article 12-1 of the Tax Collection Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax (加值型及非加值型營業稅法), commonly administered as 'Business Tax' (營業稅)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$0 for limited liability corporations — the JV must complete tax registration and Business Tax (VAT) registration within 15 days of commencement, regardless of revenue; only unincorporated micro-operators selling services with average monthly turnover below NT$40,000 (or goods below NT$80,000) may be exempted from full VAT-invoice issuance and are instead taxed under the special 1% small-business operator regime; a corporate EMR SaaS exporter cannot claim this de minimis regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates Uniform Invoice (統一發票) issuance for all VAT-registered enterprises. The JV must adopt the MOF e-Invoice Integration Platform by transmitting e-invoice XML data through the Turnkey endpoint or a certified Value-Added Center. B2B and B2C cloud-invoice data must be transmitted to the platform within 48 hours of issuance; the platform validates the invoice serial numbers and, for B2C consumer invoices, auto-generates a two-digit random code. Zero-rated export invoices are identified by a special export/zero-rating code section and do not undergo the same domestic consumer clearance, but remain subject to the bi-monthly consolidated VAT return and export documentation review requirement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Optional clarifying field — not part of schema; omitted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7, Item 2 of the Business Tax Act, the EMR SaaS service supplied by the Taiwan JV qualifies for the 0% VAT rate as a service provided in the Taiwan area but used abroad, provided: (i) the recipient is a foreign-located medical clinic or foreign enterprise; (ii) the contract, governing law, and performance place evidence offshore consumption and the overseas clinic's actual use of the EMR workflow; (iii) subscriptions are invoiced to the foreign entity and collected in foreign currency; (iv) the foreign exchange proceeds are remitted to Taiwan and evidenced by an FX settlement certificate; (v) the SaaS is not substantially re-supplied or used for domestic Taiwan medical operations; and (vi) all zero-rated sales are separately reported on the bimonthly VAT return with an export document set retained. Pure software-as-a-service exports do not require a customs goods declaration, but any associated hardware/dongle shipments require a standard customs export declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Zero-rated export Uniform Invoice/e-invoice (三聯式統一發票-零稅率) issued to the foreign clinic or foreign buyer
Written EMR SaaS subscription agreement and purchase order evidencing offshore delivery, governing law, place of use, and payment schedule
Foreign exchange earnings certificate / inward remittance certificate (出口外匯收入水單) issued by an authorized Taiwan foreign-exchange bank tied to the specific export invoice
Certificate of foreign legal existence or valid tax registration of the offshore clinic/end-customer
E-Invoice platform transmission log demonstrating the zero-rated invoice record and reporting code
Commercial invoice and statement of account reflecting the recurring subscription charges and currency
Customs export declaration with Bill of Lading or Airway Bill — required only when physical hardware, medical devices, or firmware media accompany the SaaS delivery
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are audited by the National Taxation Bureau with heightened scrutiny on related-party offshore clinics, repeated refund claims exceeding input tax balances, invoice-remittance mismatches, and insufficient place-of-use evidence. Where zero-rating is disallowed or refunds are obtained by misrepresentation, the tax authority reverses the refund, assesses the underpaid 5% VAT with interest, and imposes an administrative penalty of up to five times the evaded tax under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act; deliberate fraud triggers criminal liability under Article 41 (imprisonment up to five years) with responsible corporate officers personally liable under Article 47. The full audit window for fraudulent evasion is seven years under Article 21 of the Tax Collection Act, and failure to remit export proceeds within the 180-day foreign-exchange deadline automatically shifts the supply to domestic 5% taxation with a delayed payment surcharge of 1% for every two days overdue, capped at 15% of the assessed tax.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: For a mainland China Sino-foreign equity joint venture, the principal authorities are the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, the People's Bank of China, the State Administration for Market Regulation, the Ministry of Commerce, and the relevant local branch of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. The People's Bank of China administers monetary and payment-system matters, while the State Administration of Foreign Exchange administers foreign-exchange registration, capital-account controls, current-account administration, and cross-border remittance compliance. If the Taiwan jurisdiction represents a Taiwan-resident shareholder, Taiwan-side transactions may additionally be subject to the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan), the Financial Supervisory Commission, the Ministry of Economic Affairs, and cross-strait investment and remittance rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese renminbi is generally convertible for genuine current-account transactions, including bona fide trade in goods and services, subject to bank-level authenticity, anti-money-laundering, tax, customs, and transaction-document reviews. Capital-account convertibility is controlled rather than unrestricted. Equity capital contributions, shareholder loans, dividends, liquidation proceeds, intercompany financing, and other capital transactions require the relevant investment registration, foreign-exchange registration, bank verification, and permitted-use analysis. A foreign-invested enterprise may normally open foreign-exchange capital accounts and settle or use capital funds through an authorized bank, but funds must be used for permitted business purposes and may not be used for prohibited securities investment, real-estate speculation, direct lending to unrelated parties, or other restricted purposes. Profit remittance generally requires audited financial statements, board or shareholder approval of distributable profits, tax clearance or evidence of tax compliance, statutory reserve allocation, and bank review of the dividend resolution, tax documentation, and underlying financial records. Dividends cannot be remitted from accumulated losses or before legally required reserves and tax obligations are addressed. Cross-border payments involving a Taiwan-resident shareholder require additional review of investment legality, beneficial ownership, permitted business scope, cross-strait transaction restrictions, and the relevant Taiwan-side remittance controls. The medical EMR SaaS activity also requires assessment of data-localization, personal-information, cybersecurity, telecommunications, and health-sector licensing obligations before a bank will accept a foreign-related payment purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mainland China does not impose a general statutory requirement that all export proceeds be surrendered to renminbi at a fixed mandatory ratio. Export receipts may generally be retained in foreign currency in permitted current-account arrangements or settled into renminbi at the enterprise's discretion, subject to trade authenticity review, customs and foreign-exchange reporting, bank monitoring, and applicable foreign-exchange risk controls. There is no universal fixed statutory conversion percentage or blanket same-day conversion deadline for ordinary export receipts. The enterprise must ensure that export proceeds are collected through an authorized bank, properly matched to customs and trade documentation, and reported or corrected through the foreign-exchange monitoring system where required. Banks may require export contracts, invoices, customs declarations, bills of lading, collection records, tax records, and evidence explaining delayed, split, offset, or third-party payments. Export proceeds should not be routed through personal accounts, unrelated third parties, undisclosed offshore accounts, or artificial circular arrangements. Where receipts involve Taiwan, the bank may apply additional cross-strait documentation, counterparty, sanctions, and transaction-purpose checks. Any foreign-exchange settlement or retention treatment must be confirmed with the servicing bank because local implementation, enterprise classification, and transaction-risk status can affect operational requirements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for collection and payment support; Low as a substitute for a mainland China operating bank. An offshore electronic-money institution or payment service provider cannot generally bypass mainland China foreign-exchange controls, bank account requirements, tax reporting, trade authenticity review, or cross-border data obligations. Offshore card acquiring and billing may be used only where the provider is licensed for the relevant services, the merchant-of-record structure is documented, customer funds are segregated as required, and the arrangement does not constitute unlicensed mainland payment clearing, deposit-taking, foreign-exchange dealing, or illegal fund transfer. Stripe or another offshore processor may face mainland availability, settlement, restricted-industry, cross-border data, chargeback, and beneficial-owner limitations. A mainland payment institution or authorized bank is normally required for domestic RMB collection. The company should maintain a bank-led settlement structure, conduct customer and counterparty screening, reconcile processor reports to invoices, and document the tax and foreign-exchange treatment of every settlement flow.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mainland banks commonly require in-person verification of the legal representative, authorized signatory, beneficial owner, or principal controller and may conduct a site visit before activating accounts or higher-risk functions. Remote onboarding is not uniformly prohibited, but it is bank-specific and generally limited to preliminary collection of documents or selected low-risk services. A foreign director or Taiwan-resident shareholder may be permitted to complete notarized, legalized, apostilled, or consularly authenticated documents, depending on the place of issuance and the bank's policy, but the bank may still require a physical interview, video interview, local representative, or branch visit. The company should expect original or certified copies of constitutional documents, incorporation certificates, business licenses, tax registrations, ownership charts, passports or identity documents, proof of address, board resolutions, specimen signatures, lease evidence, business-plan materials, customer and supplier contracts, source-of-funds evidence, and licensing documents. Account activation, foreign-exchange capital registration, online banking, corporate cards, international settlements, and payment-processor connectivity may each require separate verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ownership chain involving a Taiwan-resident shareholder, nominee shareholder, offshore holding company, trust, or layered special-purpose vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents for every ownership layer; complete ownership and control chart to the ultimate natural-person beneficial owners; shareholder registers; investment agreements; identity and address documents; Taiwan-side and mainland-side investment approvals or registrations; beneficial-owner declarations; explanation of voting rights, board appointment rights, and economic interests; independent source-of-funds evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the registered business scope and the proposed EMR, clinical workflow, cloud, medical, or data-processing activities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current business license; detailed product description; software architecture; customer contract templates; regulatory classification memorandum; applicable value-added telecommunications, software, medical-device, health-information, cybersecurity, and data-processing permits or filing evidence; written confirmation of activities that are excluded from the company's scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of the term medical, clinical, health, or EMR without evidence of the relevant clinical or health-sector authorization
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product functionality analysis distinguishing administrative software from regulated medical-device or diagnostic functionality; customer implementation statement; medical institution customer licenses; software registration or filing records where applicable; cybersecurity and personal-information compliance assessment; prohibition on diagnosis or treatment claims unless separately authorized.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border transfer or offshore hosting of patient information, personal information, or important data
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Data inventory and flow map; data-classification assessment; processing-purpose register; consent and privacy notices; personal-information impact assessment; cross-border transfer mechanism; security assessment or certification evidence where required; data-processing agreements; localization and access-control policy; incident-response plan; evidence that offshore processors cannot access restricted data without authorization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected payments from or to unrelated third parties, marketplace accounts, patient wallets, personal accounts, or Taiwan-linked counterparties without a clear commercial rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved payment-flow matrix; counterparty master file; contracts and invoices; beneficial-owner screening; third-party payment authorization; reconciliation controls; written prohibition on personal-account settlement; explanation of any payment agent, merchant-of-record, collection agent, or platform arrangement; transaction-monitoring rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large capital injection, shareholder loan, or foreign-exchange conversion inconsistent with the registered capital, business plan, or historical revenue
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board and shareholder resolutions; capital contribution agreement; registered capital and foreign-investment records; bank statements demonstrating source of funds; audited financial statements; tax filings; capitalization table; treasury forecast; permitted-use certificate; intercompany loan agreement and transfer-pricing support where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to evidence export, software-license, cloud-service, or cross-border service revenue underlying incoming foreign currency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed customer agreements; statements of work; invoices; delivery and acceptance records; software-license schedules; service-level records; usage logs; tax invoices; bank remittance advice; customs or service-trade reporting where applicable; revenue-recognition reconciliation; explanation of recurring subscription billing and refunds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, restricted-party, export-control, military-civil fusion, sensitive technology, or adverse-media exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening results for shareholders, directors, customers, suppliers, banks, and beneficial owners; end-user and end-use statements; product classification; restricted-country and restricted-party policy; export-control review; contractual compliance clauses; escalation and transaction-blocking procedures; documented remediation of any false-positive match.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete tax, accounting, social-insurance, payroll, or statutory filing history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax registration; recent tax returns; VAT filings; audited or management accounts; statutory books; payroll and social-insurance records; reconciliation of bank statements to general ledger; evidence of annual reporting; written remediation plan for any historical deficiency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requested account structure is inconsistent with regulatory account-purpose rules, including use of a capital account for operating expenses or personal transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy; account-purpose matrix; authorized-signatory schedule; approval limits; cash segregation policy; capital-fund utilization plan; bank correspondence confirming permitted uses; monthly reconciliation and internal-control certification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The investor should remit funds from an account held in the name of the registered shareholder or approved financing entity to the joint venture's designated foreign-exchange capital account or other bank-approved capital contribution account. The remittance instruction should identify the legal entity, investment or financing purpose, currency, amount, and applicable bank purpose classification. Before receipt, the company should provide the bank with the business license, investment registration or filing evidence, capital contribution agreement, board or shareholder resolution, ownership chart, source-of-funds evidence, and any required foreign-investment and foreign-exchange registration. The bank should verify the remitter against the registered investor, confirm that the funds are not from an unidentified third party, and complete the relevant foreign-exchange reporting. Capital funds should be converted or transferred only through the designated bank and only for permitted business expenditures. Shareholder loans require separate eligibility, registration, quota or leverage analysis, loan agreements, interest and tax documentation, and transfer-pricing support. For Taiwan-linked funding, the parties should separately verify Taiwan-side outward-investment and remittance permissions and mainland cross-strait investment restrictions. The company should prohibit cash funding, personal-account funding, informal netting, undisclosed third-party settlement, and circular transfers. Each inbound transfer should be reconciled to the capitalization table, bank advice, accounting entry, and statutory filing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For genuine cross-border service, software, cloud, licensing, and trade payments, the primary rail should be an authorized-bank international transfer using SWIFT MT103 or the bank's current equivalent payment message, with complete originator, beneficiary, invoice, contract, purpose, and intermediary-bank data. The bank may require tax invoices, service agreements, delivery or acceptance evidence, withholding-tax analysis, customs records where relevant, and proof that the amount is commercially reasonable. Commercial letters of credit may be used for qualifying goods transactions, generally through an irrevocable documentary letter of credit subject to the agreed UCP rules, with document presentation, discrepancy controls, sanctions screening, and settlement through the issuing and confirming banks. Documentary collections, banker's acceptances, open-account payments, and supply-chain finance may be available subject to bank approval and trade authenticity controls. Cross-border RMB settlement may be available through authorized banks and CIPS-connected institutions where the transaction, counterparty, currency, and bank eligibility qualify. The company should maintain separate payment workflows for dividends, royalties, service fees, intercompany charges, payroll, capital expenditure, refunds, and trade settlement because each category can have different tax, foreign-exchange, and supporting-document requirements. Payments to Taiwan should be screened for counterparty eligibility, permitted purpose, exchange-control requirements, and any applicable cross-strait restrictions. All payment files should preserve contracts, invoices, tax documents, approval evidence, bank advices, sanctions checks, and accounting reconciliations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized mainland bank for genuine, documented underlying exposures, subject to bank credit limits, transaction-purpose verification, maturity alignment, and evidence of the underlying receivable or payable

Foreign-exchange swaps with an authorized bank for liquidity and currency-management purposes where the transaction is linked to a permitted underlying exposure and complies with bank risk limits and applicable foreign-exchange rules

Non-deliverable forwards may be available through qualified banks for eligible currencies and documented exposures, subject to product availability, suitability, regulatory classification, counterparty limits, and settlement in the permitted currency

Plain-vanilla foreign-exchange options or option combinations may be available through qualified banks for genuine hedging purposes, subject to suitability review, documented exposure, premium funding, product-risk disclosure, and prohibitions on speculative use

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps may be available for qualifying financing exposures, subject to bank approval, accounting designation, legal documentation, collateral or credit-support requirements, and confirmation that the transaction is hedging rather than proprietary speculation

The treasury policy should require board-approved hedge limits, exposure measurement, hedge documentation, counterparty due diligence, confirmation under an appropriate master agreement, independent valuation, collateral monitoring, accounting treatment, monthly effectiveness testing, and prohibition of leveraged or speculative derivatives not supported by a genuine commercial exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) resolution record and audited annual financial statements for the calendar-year fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs – Department of Commercial Services (MOEA Company Registration One-Stop Online System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened by June 30 (within six months of the December 31 fiscal year-end); audited financial statements must be filed on the MOEA company registration platform within 15 days after AGM approval and no later than June 30 for companies with mandatory CPA audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM on time exposes the responsible person to an administrative fine of NT$10,000–NT$50,000 (approx. USD 300–1,550) with an order to convene; non-filing of the audited statement allows MOEA desk-audit action, per-day remedial fines, and adverse effect on immigration/banking compliance certificates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-seeking enterprise income tax annual return (營利事業所得稅結算申報), including CPA certification when the NT$30 million revenue threshold is crossed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance) – regional administration at the company’s registered address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 – May 31 following the tax year for calendar-year companies; the statutory filing season closes on May 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 3% of the outstanding tax for every two days of delay, capped at 15%, plus daily post-office savings interest; failure to file enables the tax authority to estimate the assessment; deliberate concealment attracts a penalty of one to three times the understated tax and possible criminal referral

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding tax statements (扣繳憑單申報) covering salaries, professional fees, rents, royalties, and cross-border service payments made to the mainland China parent or licensors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance) – regional administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 31 of the year following the payment year; recipient copies must be furnished by February 10
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Income Tax Act Art. 114 penalty: NT$1,500–NT$15,000 (approx. USD 45–465) where no withholding tax is involved; where tax is involved, a penalty of no less than 10% of the under-withheld amount plus late-payment interest

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-investment annual operations report for the Sino-Foreign equity joint venture (年度營運報告) covering business operations, shareholding structure, capital movements, and dividend distributions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (投資審議委員會)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end (by June 30 for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals: fine of NT$6,000–NT$30,000 (approx. USD 185–930); the Investment Commission may refuse or suspend subsequent investment applications and share-transfer approvals until the report is remedied

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual registration-data verification responses and statutory register audit package (company profile, directors, registered address, and register book proof)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs – Company Registration and Commercial Administration (with city/county government auditors)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven during the MOEA annual registration audit cycle; the company generally has 30 days from written notice to respond
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to respond truthfully triggers a rectification order; false declarations may lead to fines on the responsible person and correction of the register entries with administrative costs assessed against the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Related-party transaction disclosure schedule and transfer-pricing documentation for transactions with the mainland China parent (required at the NT$200 million controlled-transaction threshold)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance) – regional administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Disclosure schedule appended to the income tax return by May 31; full transfer-pricing local file is due with the extended deadline if a TP report filing extension is granted, generally by August 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: TP adjustment risk and penalty of one to three times the understated tax plus interest if pricing is not arm’s-length; failure to furnish documentation shifts the burden of proof and exposes the company to higher adjustment

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit under Company Act Art. 20 when paid-in capital reaches NT$30 million (approx. USD 1 million) or when the central competent authority so specifies; a CPA-certified income tax return is also mandatory when annual revenue (net sales plus non-operating income) exceeds NT$30 million (approx. USD 1 million); financial, insurance, and securities enterprises are audited regardless of size
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-public companies apply the Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS/Taiwan GAAP) under the Business Entity Accounting Act; publicly listed and FSC-supervised entities apply IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission. Books, vouchers, and tax records must be retained at least seven years to cover the Tax Collection Act Art. 21 assessment window (the Business Entity Accounting Act prescribes longer commercial retention).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not impose a calendar-year UBO re-filing for non-listed companies. Under Company Act Art. 22-1, every non-listed company must report the UBO dataset — directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding 10% or more — to the MOEA Company UBO Platform within 15 days of any change. Shareholding transfers that alter the 10% shareholder list must be filed event-driven, and the MOEA annually cross-checks the UBO register against tax returns and company registration records; violations carry a fine of NT$50,000 (approx. USD 1,550) per non-compliant item plus rectification orders.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–1,200 per year for a serviced office, registered business address, and company secretary/registered agent retainership in Taipei
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800–6,000 for one annual CPA audit plus income-tax return certification for a medium-size private EMR SaaS company; transfer-pricing documentation (if required) is quoted separately
